Existing Transit Service
At the present time, the privately owned "lilwaukee & Suburban Transport Corporation is the only mass transit system that serves the entire "lilwaukee Metropolitan Area. Their "Freeway Flyer" express service is a rubber-tired bus transit system that utilizes the existing freeway system between the downtown area and Milwaukee suburbs. These operations are being extended into developing areas as demand dictates.
At the present time most persons traveling to and from General Mitchell Field use their private automobile for transportation. Public transit service available at General Mitchell Field is confined to bus, taxi and limousine service. Recent field surveys by SEMRPC indicate more than 90° of all vehicles entering the passenger terminal area are private cars. Taxi and limousine service amounts of approximately 4% each of the vehicle total with less than 3% by transport bus.
The local Milwaukee & Suburban Transport Corporation presently operates frequent bus service between Milwaukee's central business district and General Mitchell Field over 6th Street, Layton Avenue and Howell Avenue. The bus trip takes about 30 minutes.
Taxi service is provided on demand by several taxical companies. Since passengers use this service from various origins, there is no one established route. Observations indicate that trips are made over the freeway system whenever possible.
Scheduled limousine service is provided between major hotels in the City of Milwaukee's downtown business district
